title: All-day event timing conversion
lede: Staff and admins can now change an event's timing mode in the same editor that already owns its date and time corrections.

stats.n: All-day event toggle, shown in the existing Date and time group
Same authenticated Admin session, event, viewport, and timed values

sections.heading: Timed event editor
sections.note: Source-control baseline and working-tree implementation were captured against the same timed Veterans Plaza Ceremony record after the requested 4:30–5:30 PM conversion.

pairs.title: Date and time
pairs.sub: The new mode control sits above the existing date/time fields without changing the timed-event workflow.
pairs.beforeCap: Before: timed dates and times, but no way to switch the event to all-day.
pairs.afterCap: After: the unchecked All-day event control and mode-specific helper copy are available in the same editor.

changes.was: The editor preserved the loaded allDay value and only sent startsAt/endsAt, so an all-day event could not become a timed event.
changes.now: The editor owns an explicit mode draft, sends a complete normalized window plus allDay when the mode changes, and keeps the crew/notification path atomic.

verification: 45 adjacent route/source-contract tests pass, including all-day conversion, reverse conversion, imported-event protection, and notification scheduling.
TypeScript, full ESLint, migration-prefix validation, and git diff checks pass.
npm run build:app and npm run verify:docs pass.
Authenticated local Admin browser proof opened Veterans Plaza Ceremony and rendered the new control with no observed console/runtime blocker.

Baseline note: the clean source-control server logged a pre-existing /api/calendar-events/[id]/credits 500 because its HEAD Prisma client lacks eventCredit; the editor capture still rendered, and the working-tree implementation had no matching browser error.
notes: Production deployment and production event read-back remain separate gates from this local source/build/browser proof.
Gear reservation windows remain independent of event timing changes, and imported calendar events remain source-owned.
